item.dc:creator: Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Yilin Zeng

item.title: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
item.description: arXiv:2611.17685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank. For the stated $1$-motives, this boundary and the unramified quotient recover the restricted local Tate pairing, with exponential radicals. Nonsplit elliptic examples, Raynaud uniformization, and a height-one positive-period bound explain the geometric range. For toric motives we construct actual periods, convergent Robba bases, and integral action matrices. A toric basis family has perfect projective/trace-zero matrix duality, including its exact integral defect. An explicit residue-zero solution operator constructs every dual Herr class. Applied componentwise, the same operator gives relative full dual lifts for general constant-lattice $1$-motives once their coefficient sequence is specified. Finally, finite-base coefficient traces realize division-tower Iwasawa cohomology for any Tate lattice, and the period cup pairing equals the arithmetic group-ring pairing.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Mohajer

item.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichm\"uller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.
item.dc:creator: Heiko Knospe, Jiahe Shen, Roger Van Peski

item.title: Rational lines on pairs of quadrics and cubic hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rational lines on smooth intersections of two quadrics and on smooth cubic hypersurfaces over number fields. For an intersection of two quadrics in $n$ variables, we prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation for the variety of lines when $n\geq 11$, and more generally for the variety of $r$-planes when $n\geq 3r+8$. In this range an $r$-plane exists over the ground field if and only if one exists over every real completion. For the variety of lines, we also prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation when $n\geq 8$, conditional on the finiteness of certain Tate-Shafarevich groups. For a smooth cubic hypersurface in $n$ variables, we prove that a line exists over the ground field when $n\geq 23$.
item.dc:creator: Tim Browning, Stephanie Chan, Nick Rome

item.title: Extreme central $L$-values of almost prime quadratic twists of elliptic curves II
item.description: arXiv:2611.17848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove lower bounds for central $L$-values of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve by discriminants with at most five prime factors. Under the rank-zero Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, these bounds give large Tate--Shafarevich groups.
item.dc:creator: Shenghao Hua

item.title: Non-vanishing of central $\rm GL_3$ L-values in the level aspect
item.description: arXiv:2611.17891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-vanishing of central standard $L$-values of spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newforms of prime level. A logarithmic M\"obius mollifier with finite inverse Euler factors, combined with a conjugate term from the functional equation, gives a non-vanishing harmonic proportion of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large prime levels. The required mixed moment is evaluated by an asymmetric approximate functional equation.
item.dc:creator: Hui Wang, Shilun Wang

item.title: Common values of linear recurrences related to Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.17962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P_u(X)=XQ(X)(X-u)+1$, where $Q(X)\in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is monic, separabel, has constant term $\pm 1$, and degree $q\ge 1$. Denote $(A_n(u))$ the linear recursive sequence having characteristic polynomial $P_u(X)$ and initial terms $A_0,\ldots,A_{q+1}\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that at least one of them is non-zero. item.dc:creator: Attila Peth\H{o}

item.title: Lower bounds on ranks of universal quadratic forms through geometry-of-numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.17965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain lower bounds for the ranks of universal forms over totally real cubic fields using techniques from geometry-of-numbers and the parametrisation of cubic rings by binary cubics due to Delone--Faddeev. Additionally, our methods give lower bounds for totally real primitive fields of any degree with codifferent generated by a totally positive element.
item.dc:creator: Mart\'i Oller

item.title: The minimal excludant of $\ell$-regular overpartitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Andrews and Newman \cite{AN1} introduced the minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition, and Aricheta and Donato \cite{AD} extended it to overpartitions. More recently, Meher \cite{Meher} and Tejash, Bhowmick and Meher \cite{TBM} studied the analogous statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions. In this article, for an integer $\ell\ge 2$, we define the minimal excludant $\omex_\ell(\pi)$ of an $\ell$-regular overpartition $\pi$ as the smallest positive integer that is not divisible by $\ell$ and does not occur as a non-overlined part of $\pi$. We study $\sm{\ell}(n)$, the sum of $\omex_\ell(\pi)$ over all $\ell$-regular overpartitions $\pi$ of $n$. We obtain generating functions for $\sm{\ell}(n)$ as eta-quotients for $\ell=2$ and $\ell=3$. Later, motivated from \cite{TBM}, we obtained explicit generating functions for $\sm{\ell}(n)$. We show that $\sm{\ell}(n)$ is weakly increasing in $n$, and we derive Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sm{2}(n)$ and $\sm{3}(n)$. We then determine the parity of both functions completely: $\sm{2}(n)$ is even for every $n\ge 1$, while $\sm{3}(n)$ is odd if and only if $n=0$ or $n$ is a centred hexagonal number. Also, we obtain for every $\ell\ge3$, $\sm{\ell}(n)$ is odd for infinitely many $n$, and the number of such $n\le X$ is $\gg\sqrt{X}$. Finally, we establish congruences for these functions modulo $3$, $4$ and $8$.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Bhowmick, Nabin Kumar Meher

item.title: Equidistribution of Gross lattices of supersingular elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.18167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a prime $p$, we consider two important families of integral quadratic lattices associated to isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}$, the lattices of endomorphisms of trace zero, and the Gross lattices of endomorphisms. We prove effective equidistribution of the shapes of these lattices as $p\to\infty$ through primes, in the arithmetic locally symmetric space of unimodular lattices up to isometry. As an application, we obtain, as $p\to\infty$, the asymptotic distribution of successive minima of these lattices. These results are proved using tools from homogeneous dynamics, in particular, the key dynamical input is a recent adelic equidistribution theorem due to Einsiedler, Margulis, Mohammadi, and Venkatesh.
item.dc:creator: Lam L. Pham

item.title: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.18218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},\Sigma},U_n^\mathrm{\'et}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{\'et}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric \'etale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $\Sigma$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.
item.dc:creator: Sa'ar Zehavi

item.title: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $\tau=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $\alpha$ satisfying $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|>(8\pi y^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(\alpha;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}\Lambda(n)e(\alpha n^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8\pi y^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(\alpha;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Z. Kh. Rakhmonov, "Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs'', Chebyshevskii Sb., 22:4 (2021), 200-224
item.dc:creator: Zarullo Rakhmonov

item.title: On Borwein polynomials with multiple roots outside the unit disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.18323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Borwein polynomial has coefficients in ${-1,0,1}$ and nonzero constant and leading coefficients. We seek Borwein polynomials having a multiple root outside the unit disk. To this end, we consider the powers $L^2$ and $L^3$ of Lehmer's polynomial $L$, which has a real root $\tau>1$. Since $L$ has exceptionally small Mahler measure, the theorem of Bombieri and Vaaler guarantees the existence of Borwein multiples of these powers. Such multiples have $\tau$ as a root of multiplicity at least 2 and 3, respectively. Mossinghoff (2003, Algorithm 3, p. 323) constructed examples that, under the substitution $x\mapsto -x$, yield such multiples. The main contribution of this paper is to determine the least possible degrees of Borwein multiples of $L^2$ and $L^3$, with and without symmetry restrictions on their coefficients, and to describe their degree spectra. For $L^2$, the minimum degree is 34 without symmetry restrictions, 38 among self-reciprocal multiples, and 41 among antireciprocal multiples. For $L^3$, the corresponding minimum degrees are 115, 115, and 117. We determine the complete degree spectra for $L^2$ and, for $L^3$, classify the degrees from 115 to 150 for which self-reciprocal or antireciprocal Borwein multiples exist, giving an explicit example for each admissible degree in each symmetry class. Further constructions yield Borwein multiples of $L^3$ in every degree $D\geq 215$, with both symmetry types for every $D\geq 231$.
item.dc:creator: Souad El Otmani, Musbahu Idris, Jean-Marc Sac-Epee

item.title: On Zhao's conjectural basis for finite multiple zeta values
item.description: arXiv:2611.18536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a conjecture by J. Zhao which states that every finite multiple zeta value associated with a nonempty index is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(k_1,\dots, k_r, 2, 1)$, where $k_i\in \{2, 3\}$. Our proof proceeds by constructing a basis for the space of formal multiple zeta values defined by the confluence relations. This approach also reduces the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture (apart from compatibility with the depth filtration) to linear independence conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values, without using motivic theory.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichiro Seki

item.title: Depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets of tame covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.17399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize DeBacker and Reeder's construction (or rather, its refinement by Kaletha) of depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets to tame covers of unramified reductive groups defined by \'etale levels. These include, in particular, all tame covers associated to Brylinski-Deligne data. We prove that our L-packets satisfy invariance of formal degrees and an appropriate notion of stability.
item.dc:creator: Nhat Hoang Le, Yifei Zhao

item.title: New Congruences for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partition in $k$-Colors
item.dc:creator: Anjelin Mariya Johnson, S. N. Fathima

item.title: Correlation distribution for a class of Niho exponents via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.17506v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $q=2^m$ for an even $m\geq 6$ and let $d=s(q-1)+1$ with $4s\equiv5\pmod{q+1}$. In this paper, the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period $q^2-1$ and its $d$-decimation is considered. The cross-correlation function takes seven values $q(i-1)-1$ for $0\leq i\leq 6$, and we determine their frequencies based on the study of low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums, which are finally expressed in terms of $K_m(1)$ and $K_m(\omega)$, where $K_m(\cdot)$ is the Kloomsterman sum on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $\omega$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_4$.
item.dc:creator: Yongbo Xia, Chunlei Li, Xiangyong Zeng, Tor Helleseth

item.title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
item.description: arXiv:2611.17584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.
item.dc:creator: Noah Kravitz

item.title: Long rational and Gaussian integer multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2611.18028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long integer multiplication is a fundamental operation in computational algebra, heavily relying on Toom--Cook and related evaluation-interpolation algorithms. Conventional wisdom dictates that multiplication on the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is reduced to standard rational integer multiplication, since $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a ring extension of $\mathbb{Z}$. We show that this approach is far from optimal and moreover inverting this established paradigm, that is reducing rational to Gaussian multiplication, leads to faster rational integer multiplication algorithms. We introduce a novel Toom--Cook framework that reduces rational long integer multiplication to Gaussian integer multiplication, yielding a strictly more efficient computational pipeline. By taking advantage of the special properties of the rational integer domain inside the Gaussian integers, we achieve a more favourable algebraic structure that reduces the overall arithmetic cost in every metric. To validate this theoretical shift, we provide a complete implementation of our algorithm. Benchmarks demonstrate that our approach outperforms the highly optimised GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) by up to 29\%, bridging a fundamental theoretical insight with significant practical improvements in high-performance computer algebra.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Spiizer, Raphael S. Steiner

item.title: The M\"obius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor
item.description: arXiv:2611.18194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular M\"obius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the M\"obius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the M\"obius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.
item.dc:creator: Madjid Mirzavaziri, Daniel Yaqubi

item.title: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18374v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying any Noetherian or finite-type assumptions. We consider gradings both by $\mathbb{Z}$ and by $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ for a fixed prime number $p$, so our $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction recovers both classical examples such as usual adic projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{ad}}$ and infinite-type, perfectoid examples such as perfectoid projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{perfd}}$. Using GAGA, we prove that the adic analytification of any projective variety $X$ over a nonarchimedean field $K$ can be described as the adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a suitable pro-graded affinoid algebra $\mathcal{A}$. Moreover, we prove that in this case $\dim X=\dim \mathcal{A}-1$. We also relate our adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction to formal models.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: Descent properties for an abelian variety with extended Galois representation
item.description: arXiv:2602.05834v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a field, $L$ a finite Galois extension of $K$, and $X$ an abelian variety defined over $L$. If $X$ is isogenous over $L$ to an abelian variety defined over $K$, then the $\ell$-adic Galois representations associated to $X$ extend to representations $\bar{\rho}_{\ell,X}:\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{L}/K)\to\mathrm{Aut}(V_\ell X)$ for every prime $\ell$. This paper aims to show that the converse is true for abelian varieties of Type I, with some supplementary conditions needed on the endomorphisms of $X$, when $L$ is either a number field or a function field of prime characteristic different from $2$.
item.dc:creator: Ludovic Felder

item.title: Deformation of the absolute Galois groups of number fields
item.description: arXiv:2607.28465v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The technical goal of this paper is to construct and study profinite monoids DG_K for number fields K such that (1) the unit group of DG_K is isomorphic to the absolute Galois group G_K; (2) the maximal abelian quotient of DG_K is isomorphic to the Deligne-Ribet monoid DR_K; (3) the idempotents of DG_K bijectively correspond to subsets of the set P_K of (finite) primes of K; (4) the maximal Galois groups G_{K, S} with restricted ramifications S all appear as maximal closed subgroups of DG_K at idempotents; (5) all maximal closed subgroups of DG_K at idempotents are of this form. We also discuss the relationship between DG_K and the p-typical Witt vectors of Borger and de Smit, where we will describe the fundamental monoid of the semi-galois category of Lambda-rings of Borger and de Smit in terms of fields of norms of the local field K_p in particular.
item.dc:creator: Takeo Uramoto

item.title: Machine learning the arithmetic of Boyd's Mahler measure conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2608.00615v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Boyd conjectured that the Mahler measure of $P_k(x,y)=x+y+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+k$ for $k$ an integer, is given by $r_kL'(E_k,0)$, where $E_k$ is the elliptic curve associated to the zero locus of $P_k$ and $r_k$ is a rational number. We study various arithmetic properties of $r_k$ using a dataset containing the first $250{,}000$ values of $k$, combining large-scale statistical analysis assisted by \textsc{Claude} with transformer-based experiments carried out using Axolver. We recover Boyd's observation that, apart from a few exceptions, $r_k$ is the reciprocal of an integer. The size of this integer is governed by the conductor of the elliptic curve. Moreover, its $p$-adic valuations display markedly different behavior according to the prime. For $p\geq5$, the observed frequencies of $v_p(r_k)=-m$, for $m\geq1$, are close to $p^{-m}$. At $p=5$, the agreement improves substantially when we restrict to curves with good reduction at $5$. For the primes $2$ and $3$, however, we find additional arithmetic structure involving congruence conditions on $k$ and the primes of bad reduction of $E_k$. Although the neural networks do not predict $r_k$ exactly, they recover significant information about its magnitude and valuations. In particular, the experiments at the prime $2$ suggest predictive relationships within the computed range that are not fully captured by the explicit predictor obtained from our statistical analysis.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. Math. Artif. Intell. 1 (2026), Art. 2, pp. 1-39
item.dc:creator: Alberto Alfarano, Pablo Bianucci, Matilde N. Lal\'{\i}n, Berend Ringeling

item.title: Asymptotic counting of integers with prime factors $p_{r^a s^b}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.19434v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p_n$ be the $n$th prime, and let $r,s\ge2$ be fixed multiplicatively independent integers. We count the integers up to $x$ whose prime factors all have the form $p_{r^a s^b}$ with integers $a,b\ge0$. Our asymptotic formula for this count has relative error $o(1)$ and is explicit down to the multiplicative constant. For $(r,s)=(2,3)$ these integers are the prime codes of the ordinals below $\omega^{\omega^2}$, so the formula settles that case of the counting problem of Vernaeve, Vindas and Weiermann.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Golafshan

item.title: Coefficient arithmetic and Mellin moments of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.10578v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the signs of logarithmic coefficients associated with the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. An explicit criterion involving a finite product determines whether all coefficients in an arithmetic progression are negative or both signs occur with positive natural density. On the sets $n=5^a m$, $5\nmid m$, negative coefficients occur with positive relative density $\delta_a^-$ at every fixed $a$. If $m_a$ is the least such $m$, we prove that both $5^{-a}\log\log(1/\delta_a^-)$ and $5^{-a}\log\log m_a$ tend to $5\log\phi/(12e^\gamma)$, where $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$ and $\gamma$ is Euler's constant. These are leading double-logarithmic asymptotics, obtained from classical results on additive and multiplicative functions. Coefficient formulas also give irrationality and nonvanishing, determine the poles and residues of generating functions for normalized Mellin moments, and imply that these generating functions are not D-finite. We conclude with applications to integrals involving zeta, Dirichlet $L$, and cusp-form $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00257v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}
item.dc:creator: Henna Koivusalo, Benjamin Ward

item.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.06041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 26 unknowns
item.description: arXiv:2611.14605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with $\deg F=4$ and $n=221$.In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=26$. We also show that $16$ existential unknowns suffice under the $abc$-conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Rational isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.14873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.
item.dc:creator: Shun Ishii, Ryotaro Sakamoto

item.title: An 'Experimental Mathematics' Approach to Stolarsky Interspersions via Automata Theory
item.description: arXiv:2502.03312v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We look at the Stolarsky interspersions (such as the Wythoff array) one more time, this time using tools from automata theory. These tools allow easy verification of many of the published results on these arrays, as well as proofs of new results.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Shallit

item.title: Sparse Modular Forms, Lattices, and Codes
item.description: arXiv:2511.13816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by sparseness conditions for holographic CFTs, we investigate sparseness of modular forms, lattices, and codes. For this we investigate the free energy of such objects as their weight, dimension or size goes to infinity. We construct families of modular forms that are sparse, such as the Eisenstein series $E_{2k}(\tau)$. We then investigate lattices that come from codes and introduce a sparseness condition for such lattices. We investigate the limit of lattices constructed from self-dual Reed-Muller codes and prove that they are sparse in this sense.
item.dc:creator: Christoph A. Keller, Ashley Winter Roberts

item.title: Weakly special varieties, Campana stacks, and Remarks on Orbifold Mordell
item.description: arXiv:2603.28745v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct the first weakly special surfaces that are not Campana-special, including the complement of the plane curve $x^2y^3 = 1$ in $\mathbb{A}^2$. We prove that the set of $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$-integral points on this surface is non-dense for every number field $K$ and finite set $S$ of finite places of $K$ if and only if Campana's Orbifold Mordell conjecture holds for $(\mathbb{G}_m, \tfrac{1}{2}[1])$. This basic example carries a natural $\mathbb{G}_m$-action, and the quotient stack is an Artin stack parametrizing points on a C-pair. This leads to the introduction of "Campana stacks", which encode morphisms of C-pairs in a manner analogous to the role of root stacks for integral points satisfying prescribed divisibility conditions.
item.dc:creator: Finn Bartsch, Ariyan Javanpeykar

item.title: On $\mathbb J$-strata with Parahoric Stabilizers in Affine Deligne-Lusztig Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2606.03062v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the $\mathbb J$-stratification of basic affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties for a minuscule cocharacter $\mu$. This stratification was introduced by Chen-Viehmann and has been expected to serve as an interesting tool for studying basic loci in Shimura varieties. We parametrize the $\mathbb J$-strata whose stabilizers in the Frobenius-twisted centralizer group are parahoric by constructing a natural bijection to combinatorial invariants called small cocharacters. We further prove that the cardinality of these sets is equal to that of a certain subset of the Weyl group orbit of $\mu$. A relationship with the weakly fully Hodge-Newton decomposability of Chen-Tong is also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Ryosuke Shimada

item.title: Supercuspidal, discrete, and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.09555v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be the group of points of a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of size $q$. For a principal congruence tower $K_n$ attached to a Lie algebra lattice $\mathcal{L}$, the supercuspidal and discrete series proportions of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors both converge, with error $O(q^{-n/4})$, to the probability that a Haar-random form in the dual lattice $\Lambda=\mathcal{L}^\vee$ is elliptic. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$, the supercuspidal limit confirms a prediction of Howe. This probability is positive, and we characterize when it is one. More generally, outside a union of congruence cells of total mass $O(q^{-n/4})$, each cell determines a common Levi class for the supercuspidal and discrete series supports of every tempered representation containing its character. The limiting mass of each class is the probability that a Haar-random form in $\Lambda$ lies in the corresponding stratum. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis, quantitative estimates for parabolic incidence maps, and a Jacquet-module argument that detects unitary exponents.
item.dc:creator: Erez Lapid, Mark Shusterman
